en.name: Limb Lengthening Surgery in India
en.shortDescription: Limb lengthening in India is planned from standing films and the actual discrepancy — paediatric distraction, adult reconstruction or selected stature lengthening — not from a generic centimetre package.
en.editorialBody:
**Limb lengthening surgery in India** is an advanced orthopaedic procedure used to gradually increase the length of a bone. It may be performed to correct a significant difference in leg length, treat certain congenital or developmental conditions, reconstruct a shortened limb after trauma or infection, correct limb deformities, or, in selected adults, increase height for cosmetic reasons.

Unlike a conventional orthopaedic operation, limb lengthening is not completed simply by cutting and immediately extending the bone. The bone is surgically divided and then gradually distracted so that new bone forms in the gap. This biological process is known as **distraction osteogenesis**.

India has specialised limb-reconstruction services that use external fixation systems and, in selected patients, internal lengthening nails. The appropriate technique depends on age, bone anatomy, amount of shortening, bone quality, soft-tissue condition, associated deformity and the reason for treatment.

GAF Healthcare publishes a paediatric [limb lengthening surgery](/costs/India/Pediatric-Orthopaedic/Limb-Lengthening-Surgery) planning range of **$12,000–$28,000** (typically **7–14 nights**, then outpatient lengthening in-city). Neighbouring [limb reconstruction surgery](/costs/India/Pediatric-Orthopaedic/Limb-Reconstruction-Surgery) is **$10,000–$25,000** (7–14 nights). Combined lengthening with deformity work may sit beside [pediatric deformity correction](/costs/India/Pediatric-Orthopaedic/Pediatric-Deformity-Correction) at **$4,500–$13,000** (4–10 nights). Adult post-traumatic shortening without a named lengthening implant is planned from [non-union repair](/costs/India/Orthopedics/Non-Union-Repair) at **$5,000–$14,000** (4–8 nights) or [fracture fixation](/costs/India/Orthopedics/Fracture-Fixation) at **$2,500–$8,000** (2–6 nights) until records show which product is honest. Adult cosmetic stature lengthening — bilateral femur or tibia nails, hotel months during distraction, and later nail removal — has no separate adult GAF sheet and is quoted after case review. US comparison for the paediatric lengthening sheet is **$50,000–$150,000**. These are planning ranges from partner hospital cost sheets, not hospital quotations.

International patients comparing [paediatric orthopaedic surgeons](/doctors/India/Pediatric-Orthopaedic) commonly start with [Delhi NCR](/doctors/India/Delhi-NCR/Pediatric-Orthopaedic/Limb-Lengthening-Surgery), [Mumbai](/doctors/India/Mumbai/Pediatric-Orthopaedic/Limb-Lengthening-Surgery), [Bengaluru](/doctors/India/Bengaluru/Pediatric-Orthopaedic/Limb-Lengthening-Surgery), [Chennai](/doctors/India/Chennai/Pediatric-Orthopaedic/Limb-Lengthening-Surgery) and [Hyderabad](/doctors/India/Hyderabad/Pediatric-Orthopaedic/Limb-Lengthening-Surgery). Adult reconstruction lists tagged to lengthening sit on [Delhi NCR](/doctors/India/Delhi-NCR/Orthopedics/Limb-Lengthening-Surgery), [Mumbai](/doctors/India/Mumbai/Orthopedics/Non-Union-Repair), [Bengaluru](/doctors/India/Bengaluru/Orthopedics/Non-Union-Repair), [Chennai](/doctors/India/Chennai/Orthopedics/Limb-Lengthening-Surgery) and [Hyderabad](/doctors/India/Hyderabad/Orthopedics/Limb-Lengthening-Surgery). Partner [paediatric orthopaedic hospitals](/hospitals/India/Pediatric-Orthopaedic) in [Delhi NCR](/hospitals/India/Delhi-NCR/Pediatric-Orthopaedic), [Mumbai](/hospitals/India/Mumbai/Pediatric-Orthopaedic) and [Bengaluru](/hospitals/India/Bengaluru/Pediatric-Orthopaedic), and [orthopaedic hospitals](/hospitals/India/Orthopedics) in [Chennai](/hospitals/India/Chennai/Orthopedics) and [Hyderabad](/hospitals/India/Hyderabad/Orthopedics), are a typical first filter. City cost sheets include [Delhi NCR](/costs/India/Delhi-NCR/Pediatric-Orthopaedic/Limb-Lengthening-Surgery), [Mumbai](/costs/India/Mumbai/Pediatric-Orthopaedic/Limb-Lengthening-Surgery), [Bengaluru](/costs/India/Bengaluru/Pediatric-Orthopaedic/Limb-Lengthening-Surgery), [Chennai](/costs/India/Chennai/Pediatric-Orthopaedic/Limb-Lengthening-Surgery) and [Hyderabad](/costs/India/Hyderabad/Pediatric-Orthopaedic/Limb-Lengthening-Surgery). Pune, Kolkata and Ahmedabad may have limb-reconstruction capacity, but they are not live GAF catalog cities on this site.

End-stage joint arthritis belongs on [Knee Replacement Surgery in India](/treatments/knee-replacement-surgery-in-india) or [Hip Replacement Surgery in India](/treatments/hip-replacement-surgery-in-india), not on a lengthening nail. Sports-knee injuries sit on [ACL Surgery in India](/treatments/acl-surgery-in-india) and [Knee Arthroscopy Surgery in India](/treatments/knee-arthroscopy-surgery-in-india). Hip-preservation keyhole work sits on [Hip Arthroscopy Surgery in India](/treatments/hip-arthroscopy-surgery-in-india). Shoulder keyhole work sits on [Shoulder Arthroscopy Surgery in India](/treatments/shoulder-arthroscopy-surgery-in-india). Named tendon laceration, Achilles or cuff repair sits on [Tendon Repair Surgery in India](/treatments/tendon-repair-surgery-in-india).

> Important: Limb lengthening is a long reconstructive programme, not a single operation. The decision should be based on a detailed assessment by an orthopaedic surgeon experienced in limb reconstruction. This page is educational and does not replace individual medical advice.

[Request a limb lengthening records review](/consult?treatment=Limb%20Lengthening%20Surgery)

## Quick Answer: Limb Lengthening Surgery in India

**Limb lengthening surgery in India is an advanced orthopaedic procedure in which a bone is surgically divided and gradually separated so that new regenerate bone forms in the gap — distraction osteogenesis. It may treat leg-length discrepancy, congenital or post-traumatic shortening, selected deformities, reconstruction, and — in carefully selected adults — cosmetic stature lengthening.**
GAF paediatric limb-lengthening planning is $12,000–$28,000 (typically 7–14 nights, then outpatient distraction in-city). Adult cosmetic programmes have no separate adult cost sheet and are quoted after case review.

**What is limb lengthening surgery?**
It is a procedure in which a bone is surgically divided and gradually separated so that new bone forms between the two segments.

**Why is limb lengthening performed?**
Common reasons include leg-length discrepancy, congenital limb shortening, post-traumatic shortening, certain skeletal disorders, deformity correction, bone reconstruction, and selected cosmetic stature-lengthening procedures.

**Which bones can be lengthened?**
The femur and tibia are the most commonly lengthened bones in the lower limb. Depending on the clinical situation, other bones can also be treated.

**How is the bone lengthened?**
The surgeon may use an external fixator or an internal lengthening nail. Internal nails are placed inside the bone and gradually lengthen it; external fixators use a frame outside the limb connected to the bone.

**How long does limb lengthening take?**
Treatment varies considerably according to the amount of lengthening, bone healing, technique, patient health, and complications. It commonly involves a distraction phase followed by a consolidation phase while the new bone strengthens.

**Is limb lengthening painful?**
Pain and discomfort can occur during and after surgery and during the lengthening process. Pain management, physiotherapy, gradual distraction, and regular monitoring are important parts of treatment.

**Can limb lengthening be performed for increasing height?**
Yes, cosmetic stature lengthening is performed in selected adults. However, it is a major orthopedic procedure with a prolonged recovery period and potentially serious complications. It should not be considered a routine cosmetic procedure.

## What Is Limb Lengthening Surgery?

Limb lengthening surgery uses the body's ability to create new bone after a controlled surgical separation of the bone.

The process begins with an **osteotomy**, in which the surgeon carefully cuts the bone while preserving as much of its blood supply and surrounding soft tissue as possible. A fixation device is then used to maintain alignment.

After an initial healing period, the two bone segments are gradually moved apart. This creates a controlled gap in which new bone, called **regenerate bone**, develops.

The gradual process is called **distraction osteogenesis**. It is fundamentally different from simply stretching or extending a bone during surgery.

The rate and amount of distraction are individualised. The surgeon monitors X-rays and the patient's clinical progress and may adjust treatment according to the quality of new bone formation and the condition of the surrounding muscles, tendons, nerves and joints.

![Adult anatomical specimen of a tibia after osteotomy, with a distraction gap filled by early regenerate bone](/uploads/treatments/limb-lengthening-distraction.webp)

[Ask whether limb lengthening is appropriate](/consult?treatment=Limb%20Lengthening%20Surgery)

## Why Is Limb Lengthening Surgery Performed?

Limb lengthening is not one single operation for one single condition. The underlying reason for treatment determines the surgical plan.

### Leg-length discrepancy

A significant difference between the lengths of the two legs can affect walking mechanics and body alignment.

Depending on the cause and magnitude of the discrepancy, treatment may involve observation, shoe modification, growth modulation in children, shortening of the longer limb, or lengthening of the shorter limb.

Limb lengthening can be considered when increasing the length of the shorter limb is appropriate. The choice depends on age, skeletal maturity, discrepancy, deformity and overall limb function.

### Congenital limb shortening

Some people are born with one limb shorter than the other or with abnormalities affecting bone development.

Limb reconstruction may involve staged lengthening, deformity correction, or a combination of procedures. The treatment plan is usually individualised over several stages rather than treated as a single operation. When the honest product is rebuilding a deficient segment rather than isolated distraction, the neighbouring sheet is [limb reconstruction surgery](/costs/India/Pediatric-Orthopaedic/Limb-Reconstruction-Surgery).

### Post-traumatic limb shortening

Fractures, bone loss, infection or previous orthopaedic surgery can leave a limb shorter than the opposite side.

In appropriately selected patients, gradual lengthening can restore part of the lost length while also addressing associated deformity. Modern internal lengthening nails have been used for selected post-traumatic cases, although anatomy, bone quality, infection status and deformity can limit their use. Adult trauma lists that are not yet a named lengthening nail may still sit on [non-union repair](/costs/India/Orthopedics/Non-Union-Repair) or [fracture fixation](/costs/India/Orthopedics/Fracture-Fixation) until films decide.

### Skeletal dysplasia

Some skeletal dysplasias are associated with short stature and disproportion between different parts of the body.

Lengthening may form part of a broader reconstructive strategy in selected patients. The timing and extent of treatment require specialised paediatric or adult limb-reconstruction expertise.

### Bone reconstruction

Distraction osteogenesis may also be used in complex reconstructive situations involving bone defects or shortening.

These cases are generally more complicated than elective stature lengthening because the surgeon may simultaneously need to manage deformity, previous infection, soft-tissue problems or nonunion.

### Limb deformity correction

Shortening may occur together with angular or rotational deformity.

In selected patients, the surgeon can combine lengthening with correction of alignment. The objective is not simply to make the bone longer but to restore useful mechanical alignment and function. Combined paediatric osteotomy work may sit on [pediatric deformity correction](/costs/India/Pediatric-Orthopaedic/Pediatric-Deformity-Correction).

### Cosmetic stature lengthening

Cosmetic stature lengthening is performed to increase height in carefully selected adults.

Published studies have reported meaningful height gains and high patient satisfaction in selected groups, but the evidence is largely based on case series and retrospective studies. Complications involving joints, muscles, nerves, bone healing, infection and fixation devices remain important considerations.

Cosmetic height lengthening should therefore be approached as major orthopaedic surgery rather than as a simple cosmetic procedure. GAF does not publish a single adult stature-lengthening tariff.

## Limb Lengthening for Medical Reasons vs Cosmetic Height Increase

These two applications should not be confused.

| Medical limb lengthening | Cosmetic stature lengthening |
| --- | --- |
| Treats a structural or functional orthopaedic problem | Intended primarily to increase height |
| May correct leg-length discrepancy | Usually performed on both lower limbs |
| Can address post-traumatic shortening | Generally performed in skeletally mature adults |
| May be combined with deformity correction | Requires careful assessment of expectations |
| Treatment benefits are primarily functional or reconstructive | Benefits are primarily related to stature and body image |
| Medical indication guides the procedure | Patient selection and informed consent are particularly important |

A 2020 systematic review of cosmetic stature lengthening involving 795 patients reported a mean final lengthening of approximately 6.7 cm across the included studies, although techniques and patient populations varied substantially. The authors also emphasised that the available evidence was heterogeneous and that clear indications and guidelines remain important.

A more recent systematic review covering studies through July 2024 reported average lengthening of approximately 67 mm across included aesthetic-limb-lengthening studies, while also documenting complications involving joints, tendons, infection, bone healing, hardware and neurovascular structures.

These figures should **not** be interpreted as a guaranteed result for an individual patient.

[Share full-length X-rays for a lengthening opinion](/consult?treatment=Limb%20Lengthening%20Surgery)

## How Does Limb Lengthening Surgery Work?

The procedure generally follows several stages.

### Stage 1: Detailed assessment

The surgeon evaluates current limb length, amount of discrepancy, femoral and tibial proportions, bone alignment, rotation, joint movement, muscle and tendon flexibility, bone quality, previous surgeries, infection history, nerve and blood-vessel status, and general medical condition.

Full-length standing X-rays and other imaging studies may be required. For cosmetic stature lengthening, the surgeon also needs to assess the proportions of the entire body rather than considering height alone.

### Stage 2: Osteotomy

The surgeon creates a controlled surgical break in the selected bone.

The goal is to preserve biological conditions that allow new bone to develop. The bone is then stabilised using an appropriate fixation system.

### Stage 3: Latency period

The patient generally has a short period after surgery before active distraction begins.

This allows early healing and formation of the biological environment required for gradual bone regeneration. The exact timing varies according to the surgical technique and individual patient.

### Stage 4: Distraction phase

The two bone segments are gradually separated.

With appropriate distraction, new bone forms between the segments. This gradual process allows the bone and surrounding soft tissues to adapt over time. Continuous or gradual lengthening creates substantially less acute soft-tissue stress than immediately lengthening the bone during surgery.

### Stage 5: Consolidation

Once the desired length has been achieved, the bone must mature and become strong enough to withstand normal loads.

This phase is called **consolidation**. The fixation device may remain in place during this period depending on the technique used.

### Stage 6: Rehabilitation

Physiotherapy is a central component of limb lengthening.

Treatment may focus on maintaining joint range of motion, preserving muscle flexibility, maintaining strength, preventing contractures, improving gait, gradually increasing weight-bearing and returning to daily activities.

The rehabilitation programme should be designed around the patient's specific bone, fixation method and progress.

## Types of Limb Lengthening Techniques

Two broad approaches are commonly used.

### Internal limb lengthening nail

An internal lengthening nail is placed inside the bone.

Modern motorised nails can gradually extend the bone from within. Some systems use a remote-control mechanism to activate the telescopic nail.

One advantage is that there is no large external frame surrounding the limb.

Hospital for Special Surgery describes internal lengthening nails and external fixation as the two principal ways of gradually lengthening bone after osteotomy.

Internal nails, however, are not suitable for every patient. The diameter and length of the bone, skeletal maturity, anatomy, deformity, bone quality and other clinical factors can influence whether an intramedullary nail is appropriate.

![Adult anatomical femur specimen with a telescopic internal lengthening nail in the canal at a midshaft osteotomy](/uploads/treatments/limb-lengthening-nail.webp)

### External fixator limb lengthening

An external fixator is a frame outside the limb.

Pins, wires or screws connect the frame to the bone. The frame can be adjusted gradually to separate the bone segments and, when necessary, correct alignment.

External fixation remains particularly useful in complex deformity correction, certain paediatric cases, small bones, significant deformities, and situations where an internal nail is not appropriate.

The main disadvantage is the presence of the external frame and the need for meticulous pin-site care. Pin-site infection is one of the most commonly reported problems associated with external fixation.

![Adult anatomical lower-leg specimen with a circular external ring fixator applied to the tibia for gradual lengthening](/uploads/treatments/limb-lengthening-frame.webp)

### Internal nail vs external fixator

| Feature | Internal lengthening nail | External fixator |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Location | Inside the bone | Outside the limb |
| External frame | No | Yes |
| Pin-site infection | Avoids traditional external pin sites | Important consideration |
| Cosmetic appearance during treatment | Generally less noticeable | External frame is visible |
| Complex deformity correction | Selected cases | Very useful |
| Paediatric open growth plates | Often unsuitable | May be used when appropriate |
| Bone anatomy requirements | Important | More flexible in some complex cases |
| Patient management | Requires regular monitoring | Requires frame and pin-site management |
| Suitability | Selected patients | Broad range of reconstruction cases |

There is no universally best technique for every patient. The surgeon should select the method according to the clinical objective rather than choosing a device simply because it is newer.

[Request a femur versus tibia lengthening plan](/consult?treatment=Limb%20Lengthening%20Surgery)

## How Much Height Can Be Gained With Limb Lengthening?

There is no single safe or appropriate amount of lengthening for every patient.

The achievable amount depends on femur or tibia, original bone length, soft-tissue flexibility, muscle and tendon tolerance, joint movement, bone quality, patient age, previous surgery, overall body proportions, fixation method and rate of bone formation.

Research in cosmetic stature lengthening has reported average gains around 6–7 cm in several systematic reviews, but individual results vary considerably.

More length is not automatically better. As the bone becomes longer, muscles, tendons, nerves, blood vessels, skin and joints must accommodate the change. Excessive lengthening can increase the risk of soft-tissue problems and functional limitations.

A surgeon should therefore establish a realistic target rather than promising a particular number of centimetres.

## Femur vs Tibia Lengthening

Both the femur and tibia can be lengthened.

### Femur lengthening

The femur is the thigh bone. Femoral lengthening may be performed for limb-length discrepancy, reconstruction, deformity correction or cosmetic stature lengthening. Internal nails are commonly considered in appropriately selected adult patients.

### Tibia lengthening

The tibia is the main weight-bearing bone of the lower leg. Tibial lengthening can be technically demanding because the ankle and surrounding soft tissues must accommodate the gradual increase in length. Ankle stiffness and equinus deformity are recognised concerns during lower-limb lengthening.

### Femur and tibia lengthening

In selected cosmetic patients, femoral and tibial lengthening may be performed as separate stages. Doing both segments is substantially more demanding than treating a single bone. The decision depends on the patient's anatomy, treatment goals, the surgeon's assessment, rehabilitation capacity and risk tolerance.

## Who Is a Candidate for Limb Lengthening Surgery?

Candidate selection is highly individualised.

For medically indicated lengthening, appropriate candidates may include patients with significant leg-length discrepancy, congenital limb shortening, post-traumatic shortening, selected skeletal dysplasias, bone defects, certain deformities associated with shortening, and selected reconstructive problems.

For cosmetic stature lengthening, the assessment is more selective. The patient should generally have reached skeletal maturity, have appropriate bone anatomy, understand the prolonged rehabilitation process, and have realistic expectations. The surgeon should also determine whether the desired outcome can be achieved without creating an unacceptable risk to function.

## Who May Not Be Suitable for Limb Lengthening?

Limb lengthening may be inappropriate or require modification in patients with certain conditions.

Potential concerns include active bone or soft-tissue infection, poor bone quality, significant uncontrolled medical disease, severe vascular problems, inadequate soft-tissue condition, certain nerve disorders, open growth plates when an adult-type internal nail is being considered, inability to participate in prolonged rehabilitation, unrealistic expectations, and anatomical limitations that make the proposed technique unsuitable.

The exact contraindications depend on the indication and the device being considered. For example, substantial deformity, narrow intramedullary canals and active infection can limit the use of internal lengthening nails.

[WhatsApp +91 90443 46292 with standing long-leg films](https://wa.me/919044346292?text=Please%20review%20my%20standing%20X-rays%20for%20limb%20lengthening%20surgery%20in%20India.)

## Evaluation Before Limb Lengthening Surgery

A comprehensive preoperative evaluation may include:

**Clinical examination.** The surgeon assesses limb alignment, joint movement, muscle tightness, gait, strength, scars, previous surgical sites and neurovascular status.

**Limb-length measurement.** Accurate measurement is essential because apparent shortening can sometimes be caused by pelvic tilt, joint deformity or other alignment problems.

**Full-length X-rays.** Standing long-leg radiographs may be used to evaluate overall alignment and limb proportions.

**CT or MRI.** Additional imaging may be required for complex deformities, previous surgery, joint pathology or other specific questions.

**Blood tests.** Routine preoperative investigations may be required depending on age and medical history.

**Infection assessment.** Patients with previous fractures, implants or bone infection may need additional investigation before reconstruction.

**Physiotherapy assessment.** Preoperative flexibility can influence the ability of muscles and joints to tolerate gradual lengthening.

## Limb Lengthening Surgery Procedure

The exact operation differs from patient to patient, but a typical treatment pathway may look like this:

1. **Preoperative planning.** The surgeon calculates the desired correction and determines the appropriate bone segment and fixation method.
2. **Anaesthesia.** The operation is performed under appropriate anaesthesia, commonly general or regional anaesthesia depending on the case.
3. **Osteotomy.** The selected bone is carefully divided.
4. **Fixation.** An internal lengthening nail or external fixation system is applied.
5. **Initial recovery.** The patient is monitored for pain, swelling, circulation, nerve function and other immediate postoperative issues.
6. **Distraction.** Gradual lengthening begins according to the surgeon's protocol.
7. **X-ray monitoring.** Regular imaging is used to evaluate alignment and regenerate bone formation.
8. **Physiotherapy.** Joint movement and muscle flexibility are maintained throughout treatment.
9. **Consolidation.** The newly formed bone strengthens.
10. **Return to normal activity.** Weight-bearing and activity are gradually increased according to bone healing and clinical recovery.

## Recovery After Limb Lengthening Surgery

Recovery is a process rather than a single date.

Hospital for Special Surgery notes that recovery generally includes a **distraction phase** followed by a **consolidation phase**, with physiotherapy playing an important role in maintaining joint flexibility and muscle strength.

The timeline varies significantly between patients. Factors influencing recovery include amount of lengthening, bone being lengthened, fixation method, bone regeneration, patient age, overall health, physiotherapy compliance, weight-bearing restrictions and complications.

Patients should expect regular clinical appointments and imaging. GAF paediatric planning notes **7–14 nights** for the index admission, then an in-city outpatient period for distraction. Adult cosmetic programmes often require months of monitoring; flying during active distraction is often inappropriate.

[Plan an international limb lengthening stay](/consult?treatment=Limb%20Lengthening%20Surgery)

## Physiotherapy After Limb Lengthening

Physiotherapy is not optional simply because the bone is being lengthened successfully. The surrounding soft tissues are also adapting.

A rehabilitation programme may include knee range-of-motion exercises, hip mobility, ankle dorsiflexion, hamstring stretching, quadriceps strengthening, calf stretching, core strengthening, gait training, gradual weight-bearing and functional rehabilitation.

The precise exercises should be prescribed by the treating orthopaedic and physiotherapy team. Failure to maintain joint movement can contribute to stiffness and contractures.

![Adult patient in physiotherapy after tibial lengthening, with a circular frame in place while ankle dorsiflexion is assisted](/uploads/treatments/limb-lengthening-physio.webp)

## Pain During Limb Lengthening

Pain varies between patients.

The surgical procedure itself causes postoperative pain, while the subsequent distraction phase can produce discomfort as the bone and soft tissues adapt.

Pain may be influenced by rate of distraction, amount of lengthening, bone segment, muscle tightness, nerve irritation, fixation method and individual pain sensitivity.

Severe, increasing or unusual pain should not simply be considered part of normal recovery.

New severe pain, numbness, weakness, swelling, fever, wound or pin-site drainage, sudden chest pain, breathlessness, or a swollen painful calf should be assessed in a **local emergency department**, not by WhatsApp. Those symptoms can indicate nerve stretch, deep infection, pulmonary embolism or DVT.

## Risks and Complications of Limb Lengthening Surgery

Limb lengthening is a complex procedure with recognised risks.

**Infection.** External fixation carries a risk of pin-site infection. More serious infections can involve deeper tissues or bone.

**Joint stiffness.** The knee, ankle or hip may become stiff during treatment.

**Muscle contracture.** Muscles and tendons may become progressively tight as the bone lengthens.

**Nerve irritation or injury.** Nerves can be affected by stretching or compression during lengthening.

**Blood-vessel complications.** Neurovascular structures must be monitored carefully because gradual lengthening places stress on surrounding tissues.

**Delayed bone healing.** The regenerate may develop more slowly than expected.

**Premature consolidation.** Bone can become sufficiently mature before the desired amount of lengthening is completed, potentially requiring adjustment or additional treatment.

**Nonunion.** The bone may fail to unite adequately and may require further intervention.

**Malalignment.** The bone may gradually develop angular or rotational deformity during treatment.

**Regenerate deformity.** Newly formed bone can deform if it is not adequately supported while it matures.

**Hardware problems.** Internal nails, screws or external fixation components can fail, migrate, bend or require revision.

**Blood clots.** As with other major orthopaedic procedures, venous thromboembolism is a potential risk.

**Additional surgery.** Some patients require unplanned procedures to address complications or problems during treatment.

A systematic review and meta-analysis of cosmetic limb lengthening emphasises that both external fixation and internal nailing can produce complications, even though patient satisfaction is often reported as high in published series.

## Is Limb Lengthening Surgery Safe?

Limb lengthening can be performed successfully in appropriately selected patients by experienced orthopaedic teams, but it should not be described as risk-free.

The level of risk depends on the reason for surgery, amount of lengthening, surgical method, patient health, bone quality, previous operations and rehabilitation.

A 2020 systematic review of cosmetic stature lengthening found favourable functional outcomes and satisfaction in published studies but also identified problems such as ankle equinus, pin-site infection, regenerate deformity, and subtalar stiffness or deformity.

More recent evidence continues to report complications involving infection, joint and tendon problems, bone healing, hardware and neurovascular structures.

The appropriate question is therefore not simply "Is limb lengthening safe?"

A more useful question is: "Is limb lengthening appropriate for this patient, and what are the expected benefits, risks, alternatives and rehabilitation requirements?"

## Limb Lengthening Surgery Cost in India

The cost of limb lengthening surgery in India varies substantially.

There is no single reliable price applicable to every patient because the treatment may involve different implants, surgical techniques, hospitalisation periods, imaging requirements, physiotherapy and sometimes additional procedures.

Major factors affecting cost include type of limb lengthening device, internal nail or external fixator, femur or tibia, one or both limbs, amount of lengthening, complexity of deformity, surgeon and hospital, implant manufacturer, hospital stay, physiotherapy, diagnostic imaging, follow-up visits, management of complications and need for implant removal.

For international patients, the total medical-tourism budget should also account for accommodation, local transportation, attendant expenses, visa-related costs and the length of stay in India. Outpatient distraction lodging is usually outside the hospital band.

**Limb lengthening surgery cost in India: get a personalised estimate based on diagnosis, technique, implant and planned amount of lengthening.**

GAF paediatric [limb lengthening](/costs/India/Pediatric-Orthopaedic/Limb-Lengthening-Surgery) planning is **$12,000–$28,000** versus a US comparison of **$50,000–$150,000**. That sheet covers a child's discrepancy programme, not a bilateral adult cosmetic nail package. Adult cosmetic stature lengthening and complex adult reconstruction are quoted after medical-record review.

[Request a limb lengthening cost estimate](/consult?treatment=Limb%20Lengthening%20Surgery)

[WhatsApp +91 90443 46292 for an itemised lengthening estimate](https://wa.me/919044346292?text=Please%20share%20an%20itemised%20planning%20estimate%20for%20limb%20lengthening%20surgery%20in%20India.)

## What Is Included in the Cost?

Depending on the hospital and treatment plan, a quotation may include surgeon fees, anaesthesia, operating-room charges, implant or fixation device, hospitalisation, routine medicines, initial investigations, postoperative imaging, physiotherapy during hospitalisation and follow-up consultations.

Some packages may exclude additional surgery, complication management, extended hospitalisation, long-term physiotherapy, implant removal, accommodation outside hospital, international travel and personal expenses.

International patients should request a written estimate specifying what is included and excluded. Ask how many centimetres are priced, whether outpatient frame adjustments are included, and whether frame or nail removal is a second sitting.

## Why Do International Patients Consider India for Limb Lengthening?

India has a large orthopaedic healthcare sector and provides treatment across multiple levels of complexity.

For limb lengthening, however, the most important consideration is not simply the country or hospital.

The key issue is access to an orthopaedic team with experience in limb reconstruction, distraction osteogenesis, external fixation, internal lengthening nails, complex deformity correction, bone-healing problems and rehabilitation.

A patient travelling from another country should ask specifically about the surgeon's experience with the **exact type of lengthening being considered**.

## Best Hospitals for Limb Lengthening Surgery in India

The phrase "best hospital" can be misleading because limb lengthening is highly specialised and outcomes depend on the surgeon, technique, patient selection, rehabilitation and complexity of the case.

When evaluating hospitals in India, international patients should look for a dedicated orthopaedic department, limb-reconstruction expertise, experienced surgeons, advanced imaging, modern operating rooms, ICU and emergency support when required, physiotherapy facilities, infection-control protocols, access to rehabilitation, experience managing complications, and structured international-patient services.

GAF Healthcare can help international patients identify appropriate orthopaedic centres based on the diagnosis and required procedure rather than simply recommending a hospital by name.

Catalog hospitals currently affiliated with tagged lengthening or reconstruction lists include Fortis Escorts Heart Institute and Artemis Hospital in Delhi NCR, Max Smart Super Speciality Hospital in Saket, Apollo Hospitals in Navi Mumbai, Gleneagles HealthCity Chennai, Rela Hospital in Chennai for reconstruction, and KIMS Hospitals in Secunderabad. ## Choosing a Limb Lengthening Surgeon in India

The surgeon is one of the most important factors in the treatment decision.

Patients should ask how frequently the surgeon performs limb lengthening, how many cases involve the femur and tibia, whether they perform internal and external lengthening, whether they treat complex deformities, which implant systems they use, what the physiotherapy protocol is, how frequently X-rays will be performed, what happens if the bone does not heal as expected, how complications are managed, and who will provide follow-up after the international patient returns home.

The Limb Lengthening and Reconstruction Society describes limb reconstruction as a specialised field involving limb lengthening, deformity correction, complex trauma reconstruction and related conditions.

## Limb Lengthening for International Patients

International patients should plan more than the operation itself.

A typical medical-tourism pathway may include:

1. **Medical record submission.** Send previous X-rays, CT scans, operative reports, diagnosis details, medical history and current medications.
2. **Specialist review.** The orthopaedic team reviews the records and determines whether an in-person assessment is required before recommending treatment.
3. **Treatment planning.** The surgeon determines the appropriate bone, technique, target correction and expected rehabilitation.
4. **Cost estimate.** The hospital provides a quotation based on the planned treatment.
5. **Travel planning.** The patient coordinates visa, flights, accommodation and attendant arrangements.
6. **In-person evaluation.** Final measurements and imaging are usually performed after arrival.
7. **Surgery.** The procedure is performed after the surgical plan has been confirmed.
8. **Rehabilitation.** The patient follows a structured physiotherapy and follow-up programme.
9. **Continued monitoring.** X-rays and clinical examinations are required throughout distraction and consolidation.
10. **Return-home planning.** The treating team should provide clear instructions regarding weight-bearing, physiotherapy, wound or pin care, medications, warning signs and follow-up imaging.

## How Long Should an International Patient Stay in India?

There is no universal stay duration.

Limb lengthening requires repeated monitoring, so patients should not plan their trip around the assumption that they can have surgery and immediately return home.

The appropriate period depends on amount of lengthening, fixation method, medical indication, bone healing, physiotherapy requirements, postoperative complications and availability of follow-up care at home.

GAF paediatric planning covers **7–14 nights** in hospital for the index sitting, then in-city outpatient distraction. Adult cosmetic programmes often need a much longer base in India. For patients returning to another country, GAF Healthcare can coordinate communication between the Indian orthopaedic team and the patient's local doctor or physiotherapist when appropriate.

## Can Patients Walk After Limb Lengthening Surgery?

Walking restrictions depend on the surgical technique and surgeon's protocol.

Some internal lengthening nails permit controlled weight-bearing, while other situations require more protection. External fixation protocols also vary.

Hospital for Special Surgery notes that many patients progress to walking without crutches after a period of recovery, but the timing varies according to the amount of lengthening and individual healing.

Patients should never increase weight-bearing simply because pain has decreased. The bone must be sufficiently strong, and the treating surgeon should determine when progression is appropriate.

## Can Limb Lengthening Affect Normal Walking?

The objective of reconstructive limb lengthening is to achieve a functional limb.

However, temporary gait changes are common during treatment because of pain, weakness, restricted joint movement, external frames or weight-bearing restrictions. Contractures and joint stiffness can also affect function.

Published research has identified joint and tendon complications as important issues in aesthetic limb lengthening. Appropriate patient selection and consistent physiotherapy are therefore important.

## Does Limb Lengthening Leave Scars?

Yes.

The size and location of scars depend on the surgical approach and fixation method. Internal lengthening nails generally require surgical incisions for insertion and locking screws. External fixation involves multiple pin or wire sites and can leave several small scars. Previous surgery, infection, wound problems and additional procedures may increase scarring.

## Can the Lengthening Nail Be Removed?

In some patients, the internal lengthening nail is later removed after the bone has adequately consolidated.

Whether removal is necessary depends on the implant, patient, symptoms, surgeon's preference and clinical circumstances. Implant removal is itself another surgical procedure and should therefore be discussed as part of the initial treatment plan and quotation.

## How Long Does the New Bone Take to Heal?

Bone healing varies between individuals.

The treatment has two major biological periods. **Distraction:** the bone segments are gradually separated. **Consolidation:** the newly formed bone becomes stronger and more mature.

The amount of lengthening, bone involved, patient health, nutrition, smoking status, mechanical stability and individual biology can influence healing. External fixation studies have historically measured treatment duration in relation to centimetres of lengthening, but these figures vary considerably between patients and techniques.

## Nutrition During Limb Lengthening

Good nutrition supports recovery. Patients should maintain adequate intake of protein, calcium, vitamin D, iron when deficient, and other essential micronutrients.

The specific supplementation plan should be based on the patient's nutritional status and treating physician's advice.

Smoking is an important concern because tobacco exposure can adversely affect bone healing. Patients should discuss smoking and nicotine use with their orthopaedic team before surgery.

## Psychological Considerations in Cosmetic Stature Lengthening

Cosmetic stature lengthening requires careful consideration of expectations.

The surgery can involve months of physical rehabilitation, restricted mobility, discomfort, repeated imaging and uncertainty about the final recovery.

Patients should understand that the procedure is major surgery, height gain is not guaranteed to a specific number, complications can require additional surgery, recovery can be prolonged, the result may not perfectly match expectations, and psychological support may be useful for some patients.

Published literature reports improvements in body image and satisfaction in many selected patients, but the evidence is heterogeneous and does not mean that every patient will experience the same psychological outcome.

## Questions to Ask Before Limb Lengthening Surgery

Before committing to treatment, patients should ask the surgeon:

**About the diagnosis.** Why do I need limb lengthening? Is there an alternative treatment? What happens if I do nothing?

**About the procedure.** Which bone will be lengthened? How many centimetres are realistically planned? Which device will be used? Why is this device appropriate for me?

**About recovery.** How long will distraction take? How long might consolidation take? How often will I need X-rays? How frequently will I need physiotherapy?

**About risks.** What are my individual risk factors? What complications are most relevant to my case? What happens if the bone does not heal? Could I require another operation?

**About international treatment.** How long should I remain in India? Where should I stay during recovery? Can my local physiotherapist coordinate with the Indian team? How will follow-up be managed after I return home?

## Alternatives to Limb Lengthening Surgery

Limb lengthening is not always the first treatment.

Depending on the condition, alternatives may include observation, shoe lifts, orthotic devices, physiotherapy, growth modulation in children, epiphysiodesis in selected growing patients, shortening of the longer limb, acute deformity correction and other reconstructive procedures.

The appropriate option depends on the patient's age, discrepancy, skeletal maturity, symptoms, anatomy and treatment objectives.

## Frequently Asked Questions About Limb Lengthening Surgery in India

### Is limb lengthening surgery available in India?

Yes. Limb lengthening and reconstruction procedures are performed in specialised orthopaedic centres in India using external fixation and, in appropriately selected patients, internal lengthening nails.

### Is limb lengthening surgery painful?

Pain and discomfort are possible after surgery and during the lengthening process. Pain management and physiotherapy form important parts of postoperative care.

### How many centimetres can limb lengthening achieve?

There is no universal safe number. Published cosmetic-lengthening studies have reported average gains of approximately 6–7 cm, but individual outcomes vary and larger lengthening can increase soft-tissue and functional risks.

### Can I increase my height through limb lengthening?

Selected skeletally mature adults can undergo cosmetic stature lengthening. However, the procedure is major orthopaedic surgery and requires prolonged rehabilitation and careful assessment of risks and expectations.

### Is internal lengthening better than an external fixator?

Neither technique is universally better. Internal nails can reduce some problems associated with external fixation, while external fixation remains valuable for complex deformities, certain paediatric cases, and situations where an internal nail is unsuitable.

### How long does limb lengthening take?

The total treatment period depends on the amount of lengthening, bone healing, fixation method, rehabilitation and complications. The treatment includes both distraction and consolidation phases.

### Can both legs be lengthened?

Yes, bilateral lower-limb lengthening may be performed in selected cases, particularly in cosmetic stature lengthening. The treatment is considerably more demanding than lengthening one limb.

### Is limb lengthening permanent?

Once the newly formed bone has completely consolidated, the achieved bone length is intended to be permanent. However, the final functional result depends on bone healing, alignment, soft-tissue adaptation and rehabilitation.

### Can limb lengthening correct a leg-length discrepancy?

Yes. Gradual lengthening is an established method for treating selected leg-length discrepancies. The exact treatment depends on the cause and size of the discrepancy.

### Can limb lengthening correct deformity?

In selected patients, lengthening can be combined with correction of angular or rotational deformity.

### Is limb lengthening safe for children?

Children require a different approach because their growth plates may still be open. The technique and timing must be determined by a paediatric orthopaedic or limb-reconstruction specialist. GAF paediatric planning is **$12,000–$28,000**.

### Can I return to sports after limb lengthening?

Return to sports depends on complete bone healing, joint movement, muscle strength, gait and the surgeon's assessment. High-impact activity should not be resumed simply because the distraction phase has finished.

### Does cosmetic limb lengthening affect walking?

The objective is to preserve function, but temporary gait changes and complications such as joint stiffness or contracture can occur. Appropriate rehabilitation is essential.

### Does limb lengthening cause nerve problems?

Nerve irritation or injury is a recognised potential complication because nerves must adapt to gradual changes in limb length. New numbness, weakness or severe pain should be reported immediately. Sudden loss of circulation or rapidly worsening neurological change belongs in a local emergency department.

### Can limb lengthening cause blood clots?

Major orthopaedic surgery and prolonged reduced mobility can increase the risk of venous thromboembolism. The treating team assesses individual risk and determines whether preventive measures are required. Chest pain, breathlessness or a swollen painful calf is an emergency-department problem, not a WhatsApp question.

### Will I need physiotherapy?

Yes. Physiotherapy is an important part of limb lengthening because maintaining joint movement and muscle flexibility helps reduce functional problems during treatment.

### How much does limb lengthening surgery cost in India?

GAF paediatric limb-lengthening planning is **$12,000–$28,000**. Neighbouring reconstruction is **$10,000–$25,000**. Adult cosmetic stature lengthening is quoted after case review. A personalised quotation is more reliable than a single generic price.

### Can international patients undergo limb lengthening surgery in India?

Yes. International patients can seek evaluation and treatment in India. However, because limb lengthening requires prolonged monitoring, travel and follow-up arrangements should be planned before surgery.

## Key Benefits of Limb Lengthening Surgery

Depending on the indication, potential benefits may include correction of leg-length discrepancy, improved limb symmetry, restoration of limb length after trauma, correction of selected deformities, reconstruction of certain bone defects, improved limb proportions, and increased height in selected cosmetic patients.

The expected benefit depends entirely on the underlying condition and treatment goal.

## Important Limitations

Limb lengthening should never be presented as a guaranteed solution.

It may involve multiple months of treatment, repeated X-rays, regular physiotherapy, restricted mobility, temporary dependence on walking aids, additional procedures, complications and long-term follow-up.

The patient's commitment to rehabilitation can be as important as the operation itself.

## Why GAF Healthcare for Limb Lengthening Surgery in India?

GAF Healthcare assists international patients seeking specialised medical treatment in India.

For limb lengthening cases, our role can include reviewing available medical records, coordinating orthopaedic specialist opinions, sharing diagnostic reports with hospitals, obtaining treatment estimates, coordinating hospital appointments, supporting medical travel planning, assisting with accommodation and local logistics, coordinating communication with the hospital, and supporting patients during their treatment journey.

Because limb lengthening is highly individualised, GAF Healthcare focuses on matching the patient's diagnosis and treatment requirement with an appropriate orthopaedic centre rather than treating the procedure as a standard package.

## Bottom Line

**Limb lengthening surgery is an advanced orthopaedic procedure that gradually increases bone length through distraction osteogenesis.**

It can be used for leg-length discrepancy, congenital or post-traumatic shortening, selected deformities, skeletal conditions, reconstruction, and — in carefully selected adults — cosmetic stature lengthening.

Modern internal lengthening nails have expanded the options available to appropriately selected patients, while external fixation remains an important tool for complex limb reconstruction.

However, limb lengthening is a long treatment process rather than a single operation. The final outcome depends on appropriate patient selection, accurate surgical planning, the chosen technique, bone regeneration, soft-tissue adaptation, physiotherapy and careful follow-up.

For international patients considering **limb lengthening surgery in India**, the most important first step is a specialist evaluation based on the patient's X-rays, medical history, limb measurements, treatment objectives and previous surgeries.

Fever with wound or pin-site drainage, sudden chest pain, breathlessness, a swollen painful calf, or new severe neurovascular change should be assessed in a local emergency department.

en.editorialBody:
**Tendon repair surgery in India** is performed to restore continuity and function when a tendon is torn, ruptured, severely damaged, or separated from its attachment. Treatment can involve direct tendon suturing, reattachment to bone, minimally invasive repair, tendon grafting, or tendon reconstruction depending on the injury.

For international patients, the appropriate procedure depends much more on which tendon is injured, how severe the damage is, how long ago the injury occurred, tissue quality, associated nerve or bone injuries, and rehabilitation requirements than on the term "tendon repair" alone.

GAF Healthcare planning for adult [tendon repair](/costs/India/Orthopedics/Tendon-Repair) is **$1,500–$5,000** (typically **outpatient or 1–2 nights**). Named [Achilles repair](/costs/India/Orthopedics/Achilles-Repair) is a different sheet: **$2,000–$6,000** (typically **1–3 nights**). Named [rotator cuff repair](/costs/India/Orthopedics/Rotator-Cuff-Repair) is **$2,800–$7,000** (typically **1–3 nights**). Combined tendon-nerve loss or staged grafting sits on [hand reconstruction](/costs/India/Orthopedics/Hand-Reconstruction) at **$3,500–$10,000** (typically **2–5 nights**). Children's lacerations or transfers use the paediatric [tendon repair surgery](/costs/India/Pediatric-Orthopaedic/Tendon-Repair-Surgery) sheet of **$1,500–$5,000**. US comparison for adult tendon repair is **$8,000–$22,000**. These are planning ranges from partner hospital cost sheets, not hospital quotations. Chronic reconstruction, multi-tendon trauma and combined nerve repair are quoted after case review.

International patients comparing [orthopaedic surgeons](/doctors/India/Orthopedics) commonly start with [Delhi NCR](/doctors/India/Delhi-NCR/Orthopedics/Tendon-Repair), [Mumbai](/doctors/India/Mumbai/Orthopedics/Tendon-Repair), [Bengaluru](/doctors/India/Bengaluru/Orthopedics/Tendon-Repair), [Chennai](/doctors/India/Chennai/Orthopedics/Tendon-Repair) and [Hyderabad](/doctors/India/Hyderabad/Orthopedics/Tendon-Repair). Achilles lists sit on [Delhi NCR](/doctors/India/Delhi-NCR/Orthopedics/Achilles-Repair), [Mumbai](/doctors/India/Mumbai/Orthopedics/Achilles-Repair), [Bengaluru](/doctors/India/Bengaluru/Orthopedics/Achilles-Repair), [Chennai](/doctors/India/Chennai/Orthopedics/Achilles-Repair) and [Hyderabad](/doctors/India/Hyderabad/Orthopedics/Achilles-Repair). Partner [orthopaedic hospitals](/hospitals/India/Orthopedics) in [Delhi NCR](/hospitals/India/Delhi-NCR/Orthopedics), [Mumbai](/hospitals/India/Mumbai/Orthopedics) and [Bengaluru](/hospitals/India/Bengaluru/Orthopedics), and in [Chennai](/hospitals/India/Chennai/Orthopedics) and [Hyderabad](/hospitals/India/Hyderabad/Orthopedics), are a typical first filter. City cost sheets include [Delhi NCR](/costs/India/Delhi-NCR/Orthopedics/Tendon-Repair), [Mumbai](/costs/India/Mumbai/Orthopedics/Tendon-Repair), [Bengaluru](/costs/India/Bengaluru/Orthopedics/Tendon-Repair), [Chennai](/costs/India/Chennai/Orthopedics/Tendon-Repair) and [Hyderabad](/costs/India/Hyderabad/Orthopedics/Tendon-Repair). Pune, Kolkata and Ahmedabad may have tendon services, but they are not live GAF catalog cities on this site.

Shoulder cuff tears that belong on a named cuff sheet sit on [Shoulder Arthroscopy Surgery in India](/treatments/shoulder-arthroscopy-surgery-in-india). Sports-knee ligaments sit on [ACL Surgery in India](/treatments/acl-surgery-in-india) and [Knee Arthroscopy Surgery in India](/treatments/knee-arthroscopy-surgery-in-india). Hip-preservation keyhole work sits on [Hip Arthroscopy Surgery in India](/treatments/hip-arthroscopy-surgery-in-india). Limb reconstruction is a different product on [Limb Lengthening Surgery in India](/treatments/limb-lengthening-surgery-in-india).

## Quick Answer: Tendon Repair Surgery in India

**Tendon repair surgery in India is a procedure used to reconnect, reattach, or reconstruct a damaged tendon and restore movement and strength. Depending on the injury, treatment may involve primary repair, reattachment to bone, minimally invasive surgery, tendon grafting, or reconstruction.**
Not every tendon injury requires surgery, and the final treatment depends on the tendon involved, severity, timing, tissue quality, associated injuries, and the patient's functional requirements. Recovery commonly takes several weeks to several months, and rehabilitation is a critical part of treatment. GAF planning for adult tendon repair is $1,500–$5,000 (typically outpatient or 1–2 nights). Named Achilles repair is $2,000–$6,000. Named rotator cuff repair is $2,800–$7,000.

**Procedure**
Repair or reconstruction of a damaged tendon.

**Common locations**
Hand, wrist, shoulder, elbow, thigh, knee, ankle and foot.

**Common techniques**
Primary repair, reattachment, minimally invasive repair, grafting, reconstruction or tendon transfer.

**Anaesthesia**
Local, regional, spinal or general depending on the tendon and procedure.

**Hospital stay**
GAF planning: **outpatient or 1–2 nights** for [tendon repair](/costs/India/Orthopedics/Tendon-Repair); **1–3 nights** for [Achilles repair](/costs/India/Orthopedics/Achilles-Repair).

**Recovery**
Often several weeks to several months. Rehabilitation is usually essential.

**International patients**
Treatment can be coordinated with consultation, imaging review, hospital admission and rehabilitation planning.

## What Is Tendon Repair Surgery?

Tendons are strong bands of connective tissue that connect muscles to bones. When a muscle contracts, the tendon transmits that force to the bone, producing movement.

A tendon can be damaged by a sharp injury, sports trauma, sudden force, repetitive stress, degeneration, or an injury in which the tendon pulls away from its attachment.

**Tendon repair surgery** aims to restore the continuity and appropriate tension of the tendon so that it can heal and eventually transmit force normally again.

The exact operation varies considerably.

- A fresh finger tendon laceration may be repaired directly with specialised sutures.
- An Achilles tendon rupture may be treated through an open or minimally invasive approach in selected patients, or without surgery in others.
- A tendon pulled away from bone may require reattachment using sutures or anchors.
- A chronic or severely damaged tendon may require grafting or reconstruction rather than simple repair.
- In some longstanding injuries, a tendon transfer may be considered when the original tendon cannot adequately restore function.

This distinction is important when comparing hospitals or treatment costs in India. "Tendon repair" is not one standardised operation.

![Adult anatomical hand specimen showing a zone II flexor tendon laceration inside the fibrous sheath](/uploads/treatments/tendon-flexor-laceration.webp)

[Ask whether tendon repair is appropriate](/consult?treatment=Tendon%20Repair)

## Which Tendons Can Be Repaired?

Tendon repair surgery may be performed on tendons throughout the body.

### Hand and wrist

Common examples include flexor tendon injuries, extensor tendon injuries, thumb tendon injuries, wrist tendon injuries, lacerations following cuts, and ruptures following trauma.

Hand tendon surgery is particularly dependent on precise repair and carefully controlled rehabilitation. The location of the injury and involvement of nerves, blood vessels, bones and tendon sheaths can significantly affect treatment. Combined tendon-nerve trauma may sit on [hand reconstruction](/costs/India/Orthopedics/Hand-Reconstruction) rather than a simple suture sheet.

### Shoulder

Some tendon injuries around the shoulder involve the rotator cuff, including supraspinatus, infraspinatus, subscapularis and teres minor.

Depending on the tear, symptoms, tissue quality and patient factors, treatment may involve physiotherapy, injections in selected situations, arthroscopic repair, or other procedures. Named cuff work belongs on the [rotator cuff repair](/costs/India/Orthopedics/Rotator-Cuff-Repair) sheet and on [Shoulder Arthroscopy Surgery in India](/treatments/shoulder-arthroscopy-surgery-in-india).

### Elbow

Tendon surgery may be considered for selected injuries involving the distal biceps tendon, triceps tendon, common extensor tendons and common flexor tendons.

![Adult anatomical elbow specimen showing a distal biceps tendon avulsed from the radial tuberosity](/uploads/treatments/tendon-biceps-avulsion.webp)

### Hip and thigh

Possible procedures include repair of selected hamstring tendon injuries, gluteal tendon tears and adductor tendon injuries.

### Knee

Tendon injuries around the knee can include patellar tendon rupture, quadriceps tendon rupture and hamstring tendon injuries. Ligament reconstruction is a different product on [ACL Surgery in India](/treatments/acl-surgery-in-india).

### Ankle and foot

Common tendon injuries include Achilles tendon rupture, peroneal tendon injuries, tibialis posterior tendon injuries and other foot and ankle tendon tears.

The Achilles tendon transfers the force of the calf muscles to the heel and plays a major role in walking, running and jumping. Named Achilles work sits on [Achilles repair](/costs/India/Orthopedics/Achilles-Repair), not on the generic tendon-repair sheet.

![Adult anatomical heel specimen showing a complete midsubstance Achilles tendon rupture with a gap between stumps](/uploads/treatments/tendon-achilles-rupture.webp)

## When Is Tendon Repair Surgery Necessary?

Not every tendon injury requires surgery.

Treatment depends on the tendon, location and severity of the injury, as well as the patient's functional requirements.

Surgery may be considered when there is a complete tendon rupture, a significant traumatic tendon laceration, tendon separation from bone, significant loss of function, persistent symptoms despite appropriate non-surgical treatment, a tendon injury associated with another injury requiring surgery, a chronic injury that cannot be managed effectively with conservative treatment, a displaced or retracted tendon, or significant functional impairment in an active patient.

A complete tendon tear does not automatically mean surgery is the only treatment. Achilles tendon rupture is one example where selected patients may receive non-operative treatment with functional rehabilitation.

## When Can Tendon Injuries Be Treated Without Surgery?

Depending on the tendon and injury, non-surgical management may include rest and activity modification, immobilisation, splinting, bracing, pain management, physiotherapy, progressive strengthening, functional rehabilitation, and treatment of an underlying inflammatory or degenerative condition.

For certain Achilles tendon ruptures, functional rehabilitation can be an alternative to surgery in appropriately selected patients.

Some degenerative tendon conditions are not primarily surgical problems. Surgery may only be considered after appropriate conservative treatment has failed or where there is a significant structural injury.

## Causes of Tendon Injuries

**Sports injuries.** Sudden acceleration, jumping, falling or forceful contraction can cause tendon rupture. Common examples include Achilles, hamstring and patellar tendon injuries.

**Accidental cuts.** A deep cut to the hand, wrist or foot can directly sever a tendon. These injuries may also damage nerves, arteries, joints or bones.

**Falls and trauma.** A sudden force applied to a limb can stretch or rupture a tendon.

**Degenerative changes.** Tendons may become weaker with age or chronic overuse, making them more vulnerable to tearing.

**Repetitive activity.** Repeated loading can contribute to tendon degeneration and, in some cases, eventual tearing.

**Tendon avulsion.** A tendon can pull away from its attachment to bone. Some avulsion injuries require surgical reattachment depending on the tendon and the patient's functional requirements.

## Symptoms of a Torn or Severely Injured Tendon

Symptoms vary according to the tendon involved.

Common symptoms include sudden or persistent pain, swelling, bruising, weakness, difficulty moving the affected joint, loss of normal movement, a snapping or popping sensation at the time of injury, visible deformity in some injuries, difficulty walking or using the hand, reduced strength and tenderness over the tendon.

A complete tendon injury may cause a noticeable loss of function. A person with a significant Achilles rupture may have difficulty pushing off with the affected foot. A flexor tendon injury in the finger can prevent normal finger flexion.

## Is a Tendon Injury an Emergency?

Some tendon injuries require prompt medical assessment, particularly open injuries.

A deep cut to the hand accompanied by loss of finger movement, numbness, pale or cold fingers, severe bleeding, or suspected damage to nerves or blood vessels should be assessed in a **local emergency department**, not by WhatsApp.

Flexor tendon injuries require assessment of the skin, bones, tendon, nerves and blood supply before the definitive repair plan is established.

Do not repeatedly test a suspected tendon injury or force the joint through movement.

## Diagnosis of Tendon Injuries

Diagnosis usually begins with a detailed history and physical examination.

The orthopaedic or hand surgeon will want to understand how the injury occurred, when it happened, whether there was a cut or blunt trauma, which movement became difficult, whether there was a popping sensation, whether numbness is present, whether the patient can actively move the affected joint, and whether there are associated injuries.

**Ultrasound** can help identify tendon tears and assess tendon continuity dynamically. It can be particularly useful for selected superficial tendon injuries.

**MRI** provides detailed information about tendon structure, the extent of tearing, retraction and surrounding soft tissues.

**X-ray** generally does not show the tendon itself but can identify fractures or certain avulsion injuries and help evaluate the bones.

For suspected Achilles rupture, ultrasound and MRI can help establish the diagnosis and assess the extent of injury when clinically appropriate.

## Types of Tendon Repair Surgery

The operation is selected according to the anatomy and condition of the injured tendon.

### Primary tendon repair

The torn tendon ends are brought together and secured using specialised sutures. This is commonly used when the injury is relatively fresh and the tendon ends can be appropriately approximated.

In hand flexor tendon injuries, the strength and smoothness of the repair are particularly important because the repaired tendon must eventually glide through a confined anatomical space.

### Tendon reattachment to bone

When a tendon has pulled away from its normal attachment, the surgeon may reattach it to bone using suture anchors, bone tunnels, sutures or other fixation methods.

### Minimally invasive tendon repair

Selected tendon injuries can be treated using smaller incisions or percutaneous techniques. Suitability depends on tendon location, injury pattern, tissue quality, surgeon experience, associated injuries and patient-specific factors.

### Tendon grafting

If the original tendon cannot be repaired directly because there is a significant gap, tissue loss or chronic damage, a tendon graft may be necessary. A graft can provide a new tendon segment to bridge the damaged area. That product often sits closer to [hand reconstruction](/costs/India/Orthopedics/Hand-Reconstruction) than to a simple suture.

### Tendon reconstruction

Chronic injuries may require reconstruction rather than simple repair because prolonged injury may lead to retraction, scar formation, muscle shortening, adhesions, joint stiffness and poor tendon tissue quality.

### Tendon transfer

When the original tendon is no longer capable of performing its function, a functioning tendon may sometimes be redirected to perform another movement. Tendon transfer is different from tendon repair and is generally considered in selected severe or longstanding tendon dysfunction.

## Tendon Repair Surgery: Step-by-Step

Although the exact procedure varies, a typical surgical pathway includes preoperative assessment, anaesthesia (local, regional, spinal or general), surgical exposure, assessment of the tendon and associated injuries, repair or reconstruction, testing the repair for tension and movement, closure and protection in a splint, cast, brace or boot, and a structured rehabilitation programme.

## How Long Does Tendon Repair Surgery Take?

A relatively straightforward tendon repair may take around one to two hours, while complex injuries involving multiple tendons, nerves, vessels, bone injuries or reconstruction may take considerably longer. The exact operating time should be confirmed by the treating surgeon after reviewing imaging and clinical findings.

## Recovery After Tendon Repair Surgery

Recovery is not simply the time required for the surgical wound to close. A tendon needs time to biologically heal and then gradually tolerate increasing loads.

The rehabilitation programme has to balance two competing objectives: **protect the repair from excessive force while providing enough controlled movement to reduce stiffness and adhesions.**

This is particularly important for hand flexor tendon repairs, where excessive movement can risk rupture while insufficient movement can contribute to adhesions and loss of motion.

## Typical Tendon Repair Recovery Timeline

The following is a general framework rather than a universal schedule.

| Recovery stage | What may happen |
| --- | --- |
| First few days | Pain and swelling management; wound protection; immobilisation or splinting |
| First few weeks | Controlled rehabilitation according to the tendon-specific protocol |
| 4–8 weeks | Gradual increase in movement and functional activity in selected repairs |
| 8–12 weeks | Progressive strengthening may be introduced depending on healing |
| 3–6 months | Increasing functional activity; many patients continue rehabilitation |
| 6+ months | Some complex tendon injuries continue to improve beyond this point |

Some hand tendon repairs may take approximately 6–12 weeks to heal, although functional recovery can continue beyond that period.

For sports-related tendon injuries, return to sport should not be determined only by the calendar. Strength, range of motion, tendon function and sport-specific testing may also be relevant.

## Physiotherapy After Tendon Repair

Rehabilitation is one of the most important parts of tendon repair treatment.

Depending on the tendon, therapy may include controlled range-of-motion exercises, splint management, progressive strengthening, scar management, tendon-gliding exercises, joint mobility exercises, functional retraining, balance and proprioception work, and sport-specific rehabilitation.

For flexor tendon repairs, rehabilitation protocols have evolved considerably, with controlled early movement used in appropriately selected patients to balance tendon healing and prevention of adhesions.

The rehabilitation programme should be prescribed by the operating surgeon and appropriate therapist rather than copied from another patient's protocol.

![Adult hand in a dorsal blocking splint during tendon-gliding physiotherapy after flexor tendon repair](/uploads/treatments/tendon-physio-splint.webp)

## What Can Affect Tendon Repair Recovery?

Recovery can be influenced by location of the tendon injury, complete versus partial tear, acute versus chronic injury, degree of tendon retraction, tissue quality, associated nerve or vascular injury, bone injury, infection, smoking, diabetes and other medical conditions, patient age, rehabilitation adherence, occupation, athletic demands and timing of treatment.

A simple tendon repair and a complex chronic tendon reconstruction should not be expected to follow the same recovery pathway.

## Risks and Complications of Tendon Repair Surgery

Potential risks include infection, bleeding, anaesthetic complications, nerve injury, blood-vessel injury, scar formation, adhesions, joint stiffness, weakness, persistent pain, tendon re-rupture, failure of the repair, delayed healing, reduced range of movement and the need for additional surgery.

Achilles tendon repair can be associated with wound complications, infection, sural nerve injury and venous thromboembolism. Sudden chest pain, breathlessness or a swollen painful calf after lower-limb tendon surgery belongs in a **local emergency department**, not on WhatsApp.

Hand tendon repair can be complicated by adhesions or rupture of the repair, making postoperative therapy particularly important. Pale or cold fingers, rapidly increasing pain, or wound drainage with fever also belong in an emergency department.

## What Happens If Tendon Repair Is Delayed?

A delay can sometimes allow tendon retraction, scar formation, muscle shortening, adhesion formation, joint stiffness and reduced tissue quality. This can make a later repair more technically difficult.

For some traumatic hand tendon injuries, early repair is preferred when clinically appropriate. In flexor tendon injuries, delayed presentation can change the surgical strategy and may ultimately require grafting or reconstruction rather than simple primary repair.

Not every tendon injury needs immediate surgery, so timing should be decided by the appropriate specialist.

## Questions to Ask Your Tendon Surgeon

Before agreeing to surgery, ask which tendon is injured, whether the tear is partial or complete, whether the injury can heal without surgery, why surgery is recommended, whether direct repair is possible, whether a graft or bone reattachment is needed, what anaesthesia will be used, how long immobilisation will last, when physiotherapy will begin, when walking or hand use can resume, when work and sport can resume, what the major risks are in this case, whether another operation could be needed, how many follow-up visits are required, and what rehabilitation will be needed after returning home.

## Tendon Repair vs Tendon Reconstruction vs Tendon Transfer

These terms describe different approaches.

| Procedure | Basic concept | Typical situation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tendon repair | Reconnects the patient's damaged tendon | Repairable acute tear |
| Tendon reattachment | Reconnects tendon to bone | Tendon avulsion |
| Tendon graft | Uses graft tissue to bridge a damaged segment | Significant tendon loss or chronic injury |
| Tendon reconstruction | Rebuilds tendon function using one or more techniques | Complex or longstanding injury |
| Tendon transfer | Redirects another functioning tendon | Original tendon cannot adequately restore function |

In complex hand injuries, tendon grafting or staged reconstruction may be necessary when direct repair is no longer feasible.

## Open vs Minimally Invasive Tendon Repair

There is no single approach that is appropriate for every tendon injury.

Open repair allows direct visualisation and the ability to address associated injuries, and is useful in complex trauma, at the cost of a larger incision and selected wound complications.

Minimally invasive repair uses smaller incisions and may reduce some wound complications in selected procedures, but it is not suitable for every injury and associated injuries may require a more extensive approach.

The choice should be based on anatomy and evidence for the specific tendon rather than the assumption that minimally invasive surgery is automatically better.

## Can Tendon Repair Restore Normal Function?

The goal is to restore useful function, strength and movement, but a successful repair does not guarantee completely normal function.

Outcome depends on type of tendon, severity, timing, associated injuries, tissue quality, surgical technique, rehabilitation and patient factors. In hand tendon injuries, even technically successful surgery can leave stiffness or adhesions.

## Returning to Work and Sports After Tendon Repair

Desk-based work may resume relatively early if the affected limb can be protected. Manual work involving lifting, gripping, climbing or repetitive physical activity usually requires a longer recovery. Athletes require sport-specific rehabilitation.

A rehabilitation programme may progress through protection, mobility, strength, endurance, functional training, sport-specific drills and return to competition.

For Achilles tendon repair, research has found substantial variation in how return-to-sport readiness is assessed, highlighting the importance of functional measures rather than relying solely on a predetermined number of months.
